zh: 大家好，我是余秋雨，我们继续讲课。我前面讲到，小人如此嚣张，我们对他没有办法，有我们自己的原因。我们有五个原因，使我们面对他们显得很软弱。到底该怎么办呢？他们的历史作用和现实作用都那么坏，他们的类型又是那么的繁多，他们却让真正的君子和广大的老百姓如此害怕、如此躲避，那我们对他们是毫无办法了吗？我在长期的研究当中确实得出一个结论：我们显然没有消解小人的良方。
en: Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu, and let us continue our lecture. Earlier, I explained that the reason petty opportunists (Xiaoren) act so rampant and leave us feeling helpless lies partly within ourselves. There are five reasons that make us appear quite vulnerable in the face of them. What on earth should be done? Their historical and real-world impacts have been so destructive, and their types are so diverse, causing true gentlemen and ordinary people alike to fear and avoid them to such a degree. Are we truly left without any recourse against them? Through my long-term research, I have indeed reached a conclusion: we clearly possess no miraculous prescription for eradicating petty exploiters.

zh: 通过修行，不断扩大君子的队伍
en: Continuously Expanding the Ranks of Junzi Through Self-Cultivation

zh: 在这个问题上，我们能做的事情不太多。我们首先能做的，就是要不断地扩大君子的队伍，改变君子和小人在数量上的对比。一定还需要有一批比较纯粹的君子，不受任何小人生态的诱惑，这点很重要。连我们的朋友们，如果你们心底都有小人心态的话，那么我们努力地通过我们的修行，把小人心态慢慢地驱除掉，让我们自己变成一个比较纯粹的君子，由我们再来影响他人。当我们君子的队伍慢慢地扩大以后，君子和小人的力量对比就产生了重大的差异。
en: On this matter, the practical actions we can take are rather limited. What we can do first is to steadily expand the ranks of the Junzi, shifting the quantitative balance between noble gentlemen and petty individuals. Crucially, there must be a cohort of relatively pure Junzi who remain impervious to any temptations of the toxic petty ecology; this is vital. Even if our friends harbor petty mentalities deep in their hearts, we can strive through conscious self-cultivation to purge those petty impulses, transforming ourselves into relatively authentic Junzi, who can in turn inspire and influence others. As the Junzi community gradually expands, the comparative power balance between Junzi and Xiaoren undergoes a profound transformation.

zh: 我们要用同样的逻辑让君子去驳倒小人，那是不可能的。我们只能靠我们自己的行为方式，让社会获得一种正义欣赏的依赖，慢慢地对比出小人的无聊、小人的无耻。所以在这个意义上，我们从自己的修行开始。
en: Attempting to employ reciprocal logic for Junzi to debate and defeat Xiaoren is an impossible endeavor. We can only rely on our own patterns of conduct to provide society with a standard of justice and noble beauty to lean on, gradually exposing through sheer contrast the pettiness, boredom, and shamelessness of opportunists. In this sense, we must begin with our own personal cultivation.

zh: 君子的古代标准，也就是他们和小人的原始区别，比如君子怀德、君子坦荡荡、君子求诸己、君子成人之美、君子和而不同、君子周而不比等等，这些教导对君子的风范、目标和生态做了经典的描述。但是我们还要想到，君子还有现代标准。我们不能光是古代标准，因为社会发生了很大的变化，我们的社会大大地开放了。在这个基础上，我们应该增加一系列全人类公认的价值标准，比如人权、人道、民主、自由、互助、慈善、环保等等。由此展现出更加开阔、长远、牺牲自我、温和坚毅、光明磊落的风范。当这样的风范能够更多地建立起来了，既有我们传统的标准，又有我们现代的标准，既有我们中国的君子标准，又有我们现代世界公认的价值标准加在一起，我们就会形成一个小人很难突破的坚强团队。
en: The ancient criteria of the Junzi represent the original distinction between noble gentlemen and petty individuals—such as cherishing moral virtue (huai de), maintaining open-hearted equanimity (tan dang dang), seeking blame within oneself (qiu zhu ji), facilitating the beauty in others (cheng ren zhi mei), pursuing harmony without blind conformity (he er bu tong), and fostering inclusive fellowship without cliquish bias (zhou er bu bi). These teachings provide a classic portrait of the Junzi's demeanor, aspirations, and moral ecology. However, we must also recognize that the Junzi possesses modern standards. We cannot rely solely on antiquity, for society has transformed dramatically into an open civilization. On this foundation, we should incorporate a series of universally recognized global values—such as human rights, humanitarianism, democracy, liberty, mutual aid, philanthropy, and environmental stewardship. This demonstrates a demeanor that is broader, longer-sighted, self-sacrificing, gently resilient, and transparently upright. When such a character is broadly established, combining our traditional roots with modern standards, and blending Chinese Junzi ethics with universal values, we will forge a resilient collective shield that petty opportunists cannot breach.

zh: 真正的君子行迹是一种极其美好的人生体验，只要认真投入，很快就会发现自己什么也不害怕了。过去想做君子犹豫，不就是害怕小人吗？现在真的成了君子，就不存在这种担忧。
en: The lived experience of a true Junzi is an exceptionally wonderful life journey; once you commit yourself to it wholeheartedly, you will swiftly realize that you have nothing left to fear. Previously, when you hesitated to become a Junzi, wasn't it precisely out of fear of Xiaoren? Once you have genuinely become a Junzi, such anxieties vanish altogether.

zh: 大家都讲过，我们总是会害怕小人来折腾。但是，话说回来，真正害怕的人是介乎君子和小人之间的人。如果你真正成为一个大君子的话，就像佛教里边所说的大雄，你就什么也不怕了，为什么还要怕小人？不再害怕我们曾经害怕过的一切，这是真君子的内心思想，不再害怕众口铄金，不再害怕招腥惹臭，不再害怕群蝇成阵，不再害怕阴沟暗道，不再害怕那些时时期盼着新的整人运动的那些饥渴的目光，不怕偷听，不怕恐吓，不怕狞笑，只有以更明确、更响亮的方式，在人格、人品上展示出高贵和低贱的界限，这就是我们的胜利。
en: Everyone has mentioned that we are always afraid of Xiaoren stirring up trouble. But frankly, those who are genuinely afraid are the ones trapped halfway between a Junzi and a Xiaoren. If you truly become a great Junzi—like what Buddhism calls 'Mahāvīra' (The Great Hero)—you fear nothing; why would you still fear Xiaoren? To no longer fear anything we once dreaded—that is the inner conviction of a true Junzi: no longer fearing public slander that melts gold, no longer fearing being smeared by foul stench, no longer fearing swarms of flies, no longer fearing dark subterranean trenches, no longer fearing those famished gazes ever longing for new witch hunts; fearing neither eavesdropping, nor intimidation, nor sinister sneers. Only by demonstrating the clear boundary between nobility and baseness in character and integrity in a clearer and more resonant manner can we claim our victory.

zh: 这一点，我很希望能够和我的听众能够内心沟通。我们过去牵牵扯扯的思维，主要是我们心底还有小人的痕迹，所以我们恐惧了，只要我们隔断以后，我们真的不害怕了。我们恐惧小人的那一切，如果我们下个决心咬个牙齿，我们不害怕小人，那我们真的无敌于天下。只要不害怕小人了，我们其实没什么可以真正害怕的。
en: On this point, I truly hope to connect deeply with my listeners' hearts. Our tangled, hesitant thinking in the past was primarily because traces of the Xiaoren still lingered in our hearts, which bred fear. Once we sever those ties, we truly become fearless. Confronting everything we used to dread about Xiaoren, if we steel our resolve and clench our teeth to overcome that fear, we will truly be invincible under heaven. As long as we do not fear Xiaoren, there is virtually nothing in this world we need to fear.

zh: 研究历史到现实的小人问题：警醒社会
en: Studying Xiaoren from History to Reality: Awakening Society

zh: 另外有一件具体的事情可以做，我主张大家认真地研究一下，从历史到现实的小人问题；而且，把这个问题不断地谈下去，像我一样大篇幅地谈下去，用各种方式来谈，用戏剧，用电影，用小说，用论文，用讲座，细细地分析，生动地展示，这对全社会认识小人总有好处。大家说有好处吗？有好处。大家说这个对小人没有什么警醒作用，不是这样的。我想借莫里哀的戏《吝啬鬼》，来说说这个问题。
en: Furthermore, there is a concrete step we can take: I urge everyone to earnestly study the problem of Xiaoren from history through to modern reality. Moreover, we must keep discussing this issue extensively—just as I am doing at great length—through various mediums: theater, film, novels, academic essays, and lectures, analyzing it meticulously and presenting it vividly. This will always benefit society's understanding of Xiaoren. Will it be beneficial? Yes, absolutely. Some might claim this won't awaken or deter Xiaoren, but that is not true. I'd like to invoke Molière's comedy The Miser to illustrate this point.

zh: 吝啬，其实是一个比小人的问题更小一点的、更轻一点的毛病，人人身上都有吝啬的毛病。要根治人类身上吝啬这个毛病，那是不可能的，谁也做不到。但是，莫里哀却把吝啬解剖地那么透彻、那么辛辣、那么具体，使人们在看戏以后，再次遇到吝啬，或者自己心头再一次有吝啬的萌芽产生的时候，自己猛然会觉得，好像在哪里见过。那个时候，剧场里边的笑声也会在耳边响起，那么多笑声使他们明白，现在人类的良知水平是什么样的，自己不要孤立在这个笑声之外，这个时候你的人格就悄悄地上升了一步。
en: Avarice is actually a smaller and milder defect than being a Xiaoren; everyone possesses a touch of stinginess. To completely eradicate greed and stinginess from human nature is impossible—no one can achieve that. Yet Molière dissected avarice so incisively, pungently, and concretely that after watching the play, whenever people encounter stinginess again, or feel a nascent sprout of greed stirring in their own hearts, they will suddenly realize: 'It feels as though I've seen this before.' At that moment, the laughter from the theater will echo in their ears; that collective laughter reminds them of the baseline of human conscience, prompting them not to isolate themselves outside that laughter. At that moment, one's character quietly ascends a step higher.

zh: 大家明白我从《吝啬鬼》里边举出的例子来说明小人问题了吗？对小人也是这样，大家千万不要以为小人看了我们一些小人的戏，看了我们一些小人的文章，他一定无动于衷，不是这样的。人的成分往往是交杂的，里边既有君子的成分，也有小人的成分。当小人的成分再次出现的时候，突然想起某某人写的论文当中正好描述过这种特征，或者突然想起某某人写的电视剧里边也有这样的描述，于是产生类比，产生警惕，轻轻地一笑，自己在行为上也有了收敛，有了改正。这就是像莫里哀写《吝啬鬼》一样，我们在写小人这样的作品的时候，对社会有一个警醒作用，警醒的是小人成分比较多的人。
en: Do you see the point I am making by citing The Miser to illustrate the problem of Xiaoren? The same holds true for Xiaoren: never assume that when they watch plays or read essays exposing Xiaoren, they will remain completely unaffected—that is not the case. Human nature is often mixed, containing elements of both Junzi and Xiaoren. When the Xiaoren element surfaces again, they might suddenly recall that an academic paper accurately characterized this very trait, or remember that a TV drama depicted this exact behavior. This sparks analogy and vigilance; with a light smile, they might restrain and rectify their own conduct. Just like Molière writing The Miser, when we produce works examining Xiaoren, it serves as a wake-up call to society—awakening those who carry a greater proportion of Xiaoren tendencies.

zh: 那么，也可以对于小人成分比较小的人有一些温和的启发，比较小的温和的启发，这是一件好事。这个毛病虽然比小人这个问题要轻微的多，但是，像莫里哀一样，把他们最普及的方式概括出来、袒示出来，人们一定有所启悟。
en: Meanwhile, it also provides gentle enlightenment to those with only minor Xiaoren inclinations, which is a wonderful thing. Although this flaw is much milder than full-blown petty malice, laying bare their most common behavior patterns in the open—just as Molière did—will inevitably inspire awakening in people.

zh: 所谓伟大的时代，是谁也不把小人放在眼里的时代
en: A Truly Great Era Is One Where Nobody Bother to Pay Any Mind to Xiaoren

zh: 研究小人是为了看清小人，给他们定位，以免他们继续以无序的方式出现在我们各个部位。因为他们无序的方式出现的时候，我们就难以招架了。请注意，研究仅止于研究，尽量不要与小人争吵，争吵使小人加重，研究使小人失重。这句话我要重复一遍，争吵使小人加重，研究使小人失重。
en: The purpose of studying Xiaoren is to see them clearly and delineate their boundaries, preventing them from appearing disorderly across every corner of our lives. When they appear unpredictably, we find them impossible to ward off. Please note: study should remain strictly within study; try your best never to engage in petty quarrels with them. Arguing only amplifies Xiaoren, whereas studying them renders them weightless. Let me repeat this sentence: arguing amplifies Xiaoren, while studying them renders them weightless.

zh: 好多人说，我和小人去争吵一下，结果，一方面你赢不了，因为小人的逻辑系统和君子的逻辑系统不一样，最让你感动的，你内心要流泪的东西他不感动，他的逻辑你又很难驳倒；而周围听你们争论的人，一般不会非常明确地站在你这个大而无当的空洞的逻辑的一边，不会，一般反而会对小人的语言产生同情。所以，争论只能使他们加重，而且小人在争论的时候不会仅仅用小人的语言，用的也是君子的语言，所以争论到最后，你倒反而像小人了。但是研究出人类小人的几个行为模式的话，就会使他们失重，因为他这么做了，大家就想到，我看到过，我曾经在哪个电视剧里边曾经嘲笑过，那就可以了。
en: Many people think, 'I'll just go and argue with the Xiaoren.' In reality, on one hand, you cannot win, because a Xiaoren's logic system is entirely different from that of a Junzi: the things that move you most and bring tears to your eyes leave them completely cold, and their twisted logic is very hard to refute directly. Furthermore, onlookers rarely take a firm stand with your grand, seemingly abstract logic; on the contrary, they often end up feeling sympathy for the clever rhetoric of the Xiaoren. Therefore, dispute only adds weight to them. Moreover, when arguing, a Xiaoren doesn't just use vile language; they readily adopt the high-sounding vocabulary of a Junzi, so by the end of the argument, you are the one made to look like the petty villain. However, once you analyze and articulate the behavioral patterns of humanity's petty persons, you render them weightless—because whenever they act that way, everyone recognizes: 'I've seen this before; I already laughed at this in a TV drama.' And that suffices.

zh: 有关小人的定义，小人是最难于定义的，但是，我在美国的一位学者的书上看到过一个有关小人的我认为最好的定义。他说了这么一句话，所谓伟大的时代，也就是谁也不把小人放在眼里的时代。这句话我再重复一遍，所谓伟大的时代，是谁也不把小人放在眼里的时代。这个定义十分精彩，小人总有，但是他们的地位与时代本身的重量成为反比。专制集权的政治往往是造就小人，而且造就普通民众恐惧心理，助长了小人。
en: Regarding the definition of a Xiaoren—they are the hardest to define. However, I once read what I consider the finest definition of a Xiaoren in a book by an American scholar. He stated: a truly great era is one where nobody pays any mind to Xiaoren. Let me repeat that sentence: a truly great era is one where nobody pays any mind to Xiaoren. This definition is magnificent. Xiaoren will always exist, but their status is inversely proportional to the weight of the era itself. Autocratic, totalitarian rule often breeds Xiaoren and instills fear in ordinary citizens, thereby emboldening the petty.

zh: 如果出现了一种强大的精神气压使小人在社会当中，从中心推到边上的话，从高位推到低位的话，从主宰变成多余的话，这个时代就已经开始问鼎伟大了。时间不会总是和小人站在一起，快速推进的时代节奏，无限广阔的全球视野，渐渐地使很多小人的行为越来越失去效用。前几年还在闹腾的那些小人事件，现在一看全都变成了笑话，尤其是那些折腾人著称的所谓大批判专家，那些揭秘的高手，现在连名字也被人家淡忘了。
en: If a potent spiritual atmosphere emerges that pushes Xiaoren from the center to the margins of society, from high positions to the lowest rungs, from rulers into superfluous relics, that era has already begun to aspire to greatness. Time does not indefinitely align with the petty. The accelerating pace of our era and an infinitely expansive global perspective gradually render the antics of many Xiaoren increasingly ineffective. Those petty spectacles that caused an uproar just a few years ago are now seen as mere jokes; in particular, those notorious 'great criticism experts' and 'scandal uncoverers'—even their names are already fading from memory.

zh: 但是，我们的时代与伟大显然还有距离，精神文化领域的创造者其实不少，但是仍然会被好多小人包围着。中国民众虽然也已经厌烦小人了，但是以往很多年被小人扯来扯去的视线，还没有恢复到来仰望精神文化的功能；结果，虽然小人被冷落了，精神文化最崇高的部位也被冷落着。这是一个双向冷落的过程，我相信，这个双向冷落过程是一个暂时的过程。
en: Yet, our era clearly still has a distance to go before reaching greatness. Creators in the spiritual and cultural spheres are actually numerous, yet they remain besieged by swarms of Xiaoren. Although the Chinese public has grown weary of Xiaoren, their attention—distracted and tugged back and forth by petty controversies for decades—has not yet recovered its capacity to look up at high culture. Consequently, even as Xiaoren are left out in the cold, the most sublime heights of spiritual culture are neglected as well. This is a process of mutual cold-shouldering, but I believe this mutual neglect is merely temporary.

zh: 最后，我必须补充一点，尽管小人在整体上祸害久远，但是，他们的个体生命如果来看一看的话，多数也是可怜人，包括其中最令人厌烦的文痞型小人，其实也就是一些喝了“狼奶”的失败者和忧郁者。他们，在我看来，还是有被拯救的可能。冷落他们，搁置他们，然后拯救他们，这是当代君子的责任。说到底，他们是在一个缺少关爱的环境里边长大的一群，因此，也应该受到关爱。我们鄙视的是他们以往的作恶方式，以及他们在历史上曾经有过的结合状态。我们除了揭露他们、冷落他们、鄙视他们、搁置他们，最后是拯救他们，关爱他们。谢谢！
en: Finally, I must add one point: although Xiaoren as a collective inflict prolonged harm, if you examine their individual lives, most are ultimately pitiful creatures—including the most odious cultural thugs (literary ruffians), who are essentially embittered, depressed failures reared on 'wolf's milk.' In my view, they can still be redeemed. Leaving them out in the cold, setting them aside, and ultimately redeeming them—this is the duty of modern Junzi. At the end of the day, they grew up in an environment devoid of care and love, and therefore they deserve love and care as well. What we despise is their past history of wrongdoing and the collusive structures they once formed in history. Beyond exposing them, giving them the cold shoulder, scorning them, and shelving them, our ultimate goal is to redeem them and care for them. Thank you!
